column3: Uses the PAUSE framework before prompting an AI tool — checks for Personal data, Approved tool, Understand purpose, Share minimally, Evaluate output.
Can name at least 3 AI Ethics Principles from the poster (e.g. Transparency, Accountability, Fairness, Inclusiveness, Privacy & Security).
Always uses enterprise AI tools instead of public ones like personal ChatGPT or personal Gemini for work tasks.
Locks their computer screen every single time they leave their desk, even for a quick coffee run.
Knows what SORRY stands for — Small actions, Stronger Protections (Store, Organise, Restrict, Retain, Your responsibility).
Has reported a suspicious email or potential data breach using the See It, Note It, Report It process.
Double-checks the email recipient and attachment before hitting send, especially when it contains personal data.
Knows that AI must be tested, safe, and controllable — the Reliability, Safety & Control principle.
Uses classification tags like Confidential or Secret when labelling sensitive documents.
Understands that humans remain responsible and accountable for AI outcomes, not the AI system itself.
Reviews shared folder access regularly to ensure only the right people can see sensitive files.
Knows that sensitive personal data includes biometrics, health conditions, religious beliefs and criminal records.
Uses BCC instead of CC when emailing a large group of external contacts to protect their privacy.
Can explain the Stop, Think, Protect steps — Verify, Inform, Validate, Protect, Dispose.
Knows that data breaches in Malaysia surged from 50 cases in 2022 to 644 cases in 2023.
Checks AI-generated content for hallucinations, bias, and accuracy before using it in any decision.
What does Responsible AI anchor on?
column9: Responsible AI is about AI that is dependable, reliable, explainable, and safe — anchored on trustworthiness.

column3: Which is NOT an AI Ethics Principle from the poster?
column9: The principles are Transparency, Accountability, Fairness, Inclusiveness, Privacy & Security, Reliability, and Pursuit of Human Benefit. Profitability is not one.

column3: What does the "P" in PAUSE stand for?
column9: Before you prompt, PAUSE: P = Is this Personal or sensitive data?

column3: Who remains accountable for AI decisions and outcomes?
column9: The Accountability principle: humans remain responsible for AI outcomes.

column3: Which of these is sensitive personal data under PDPA?
column9: Sensitive personal data includes political opinions, religious beliefs, criminal records, health conditions, and biometric data.

column3: What are the 3 steps in "See It. Note It. Report It."?
column9: Spot unusual activity, Record what happened, Report to Data Protection Officer immediately.

column3: The Retention Principle says you should...
column5: Delete data when its purpose is complete
column9: Keep data only as long as needed.

column3: Non-compliance with PDPA can result in fines of up to...
column9: Non-compliance with PDPA can result in fines of up to RM1 million and/or imprisonment of up to 3 years.

column3: What is the biggest data privacy risk when using public GenAI tools?
column9: Personal data, financial data, strategy documents can leak through public AI services.

column3: Which are known risks of AI becoming visible after Nov 2022?
column9: Risks like hallucinations, misinformation, plagiarism, bias, deepfakes became visible to everyone.

column3: You paste a confidential strategy document into personal ChatGPT to summarise it quickly for a presentation.
column9: Public AI services can leak your data. Use only approved enterprise AI tools.

column3: Before prompting the company AI tool, you check: Is there personal data? Am I using an approved tool? Do I understand the purpose? Am I sharing only what is needed?
column9: This is the PAUSE framework in action — the responsible way to use AI at work.

column3: You print out a customer complaint that includes their IC number and leave it on your desk while you attend a 2-hour meeting.
column9: Printed personal data left unattended can be seen or taken by anyone.

column3: An AI tool generates a market analysis report. Before sharing it with leadership, you verify the data sources, check for hallucinations, and confirm accuracy.
column9: The E in PAUSE: Evaluate the output. Check AI-generated content for accuracy, bias, and completeness.

column3: You forward a colleague HR performance review email to your personal Gmail so you can read it on the train home.
column9: Personal email is outside company security controls. Personal data must stay in approved systems only.

column3: You use the enterprise AI platform with incognito chat mode enabled, ensuring no history and no data retention.
column9: Best practice: AI Sees Nothing — incognito chat, no history, no retention.

column3: A vendor sends you an AI-powered analytics tool and asks you to upload your full employee database for a "quick demo".
column9: Never share personal data with unapproved third parties. Validate the recipient, confirm purpose, get approval first.

column3: You notice your team shared drive still has CVs from a 2019 recruitment round. You flag it for deletion following the retention schedule.
column9: Retention Principle: keep data only as long as needed.

column3: You let an AI tool make the final hiring decision without any human review because it is faster and "unbiased".
column9: Humans remain accountable for AI decisions. AI should assist, not replace human judgment.

column3: After spotting unusual data access logs, you document what happened, when it occurred, and who may be affected, then report it immediately.
column9: See It. Note It. Report It.
